transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... my husband told me I had to come. Him and... the people at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. 

But I'm not. I just... I know they've been watching my moves. They keep changing the pallet counts on my shift. They just want to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. So... that's it.
How long have you been noticing these things happening at work—like the pallet counts being changed and feeling watched—has it been days, weeks, or longer?
Um... longer. I guess... maybe eight months? Yeah, about eight months since they started watching me and... messing with the things. And the voices, too. It's been about that long.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other drugs, like methamphetamine or cocaine, during these past eight months?
No. I don't... I don't do any of that stuff. I don't drink either.
Can you tell me more about the voices you mentioned—do you actually hear sounds or people talking when no one else is around?

Um... yeah. It's... it's like a real voice. 

Like... sometimes I'll just be in the aisle at work, or... or even just folding clothes at home. And I'll hear this man's voice. Just... clear as day. He says, "Nicole, check it again." But... there's nobody there. Nobody near me.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in how you're managing daily responsibilities—like keeping up with your job performance, household tasks, or personal hygiene?

Um... yeah. Things have been... harder. 

Work isn't the same. They... they took me off the forklift. Said I couldn't do the safety-sensitive stuff anymore because I was... taking too long to check things. Slowing down the line. 

And at home... I don't know. My husband just... he says he can't rely on me like he used to. I guess I haven't been doing as much.

During these past eight months, have you had any stretches where you felt unusually sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things—or, on the other end, felt unusually energetic, elated, or like you barely needed sleep?

Um... I don't know about sad. But sometimes I guess I get... really fired up. Like nobody can slow me down. 

But... I don't know. If my husband asks just one little question about the kids, or... or my schedule... I just snap at him. It just feels like he's trying to control me.

During the times when you're not feeling especially 'fired up' or energetic—when your mood feels more normal—do you still hear that man's voice or still feel like people are watching and messing with your pallet counts?

Um... yeah, I guess so. 

Like... a little while back, things were quieter for a few weeks. I was sleeping more... not rushing around so much. But... I still heard him. Still telling me to check things. 

And... the pallets were still wrong. They were still messing with them. Even when I wasn't feeling so fired up.

Thinking back over the full eight months, would you say you've been feeling 'fired up' and irritable most of the time, or has that only happened during shorter stretches, like a few weeks here and there?

Um... mostly. 

I guess... if you look at the whole eight months, it's been more than half the time. Just... going and going. Not sleeping much. Trying to do a lot. 

And yeah... getting mad when people get in my way. It's... it's been a lot of the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient has 8 months of persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of a male voice, persecutory delusions about coworkers/pallet tampering) accompanied by a manic-like mood syndrome (elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, irritability) present for the majority of the illness duration (>half of the 8 months). Critically, the patient confirms that psychotic symptoms (voice, delusional beliefs about being watched) persisted during a period when mood symptoms had resolved ('things were quieter,' 'sleeping more'), establishing that hallucinations/delusions occurred for a sustained period in the absence of mood symptoms. No substance use or medical cause identified. This concurrent presence of mood episode for the majority of the illness with psychotic symptoms extending beyond the mood episode meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than Schizophrenia (mood symptoms are prominent and simultaneous) or Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (psychotic symptoms persist outside mood episodes).
